properties.name: Prometheus Steals Fire
properties.summary: Prometheus, a Titan, stole fire from Mount Olympus and gave it to humanity, enabling civilization. Zeus punished him by chaining him to a rock where an eagle ate his liver daily, only for it to regenerate each night. Heracles eventually freed him. The myth symbolizes the price of knowledge and defiance of divine authority.

properties.name: The Odyssey
properties.summary: After the Trojan War, Odysseus spent ten years trying to return home to Ithaca. He faced the Cyclops, Sirens, Scylla and Charybdis, and the enchantress Circe. Meanwhile, his wife Penelope fended off suitors. The epic explores nostos (homecoming), cunning over brute force, and the costs of hubris.

properties.name: Wrath of Achilles (Iliad)
properties.summary: The Iliad focuses on a few weeks during the tenth year of the Trojan War. Achilles withdraws from battle after Agamemnon takes his war prize. When Patroclus is killed by Hector, Achilles returns in devastating fury, slaying Hector and dragging his body around Troy. The poem ends with Hector's funeral.

properties.name: Twelve Labors of Heracles
properties.summary: Driven mad by Hera, Heracles killed his family. As penance, he completed twelve impossible labors: slaying the Nemean Lion, killing the Lernaean Hydra, capturing the Ceryneian Hind, and more. The final labor required him to bring Cerberus from the underworld. These trials earned him immortality.

properties.name: Orpheus and Eurydice
properties.summary: The musician Orpheus descended to the underworld to retrieve his dead wife Eurydice. His music moved Hades, who agreed to release her if Orpheus did not look back. At the last moment, Orpheus glanced back, losing Eurydice forever. The myth explores the power and limits of art and love.

properties.name: Greek Creation (Chaos to Olympians)
properties.summary: From primordial Chaos emerged Gaia (Earth), Tartarus (Abyss), and Eros (Love). Gaia bore Uranus (Sky), whose children the Titans were imprisoned until Kronos castrated his father. Zeus then overthrew Kronos, establishing the Olympian order. This succession myth mirrors Near Eastern creation patterns.

properties.name: Persephone and the Seasons
properties.summary: Hades abducted Persephone to the underworld. Her mother Demeter, goddess of harvest, caused the earth to become barren in grief. Zeus brokered a compromise: Persephone would spend part of the year below and part above. Her return brings spring; her descent brings winter.

properties.name: Romulus and Remus
properties.summary: Twin sons of Mars and the Vestal Virgin Rhea Silvia, abandoned on the Tiber and raised by a she-wolf. As adults they founded a city, but quarreled over its location. Romulus killed Remus and named the city Rome. The fratricide shadowed Roman history with themes of necessary violence.

properties.name: The Aeneid
properties.summary: After Troy fell, the hero Aeneas journeyed to Italy guided by destiny. He loved and abandoned Queen Dido of Carthage, descended to the underworld, and fought wars in Latium. His descendants would found Rome. Virgil's epic connected Roman power to Trojan heritage and divine mandate.

properties.name: RagnarÃ¶k â€” Twilight of the Gods
properties.summary: RagnarÃ¶k is the prophesied end of the Norse cosmos. Loki breaks free, the Midgard Serpent rises from the sea, Fenrir devours Odin, and Thor and the serpent kill each other. The world sinks into the sea, only to rise again green and renewed. Two human survivors repopulate the earth.

properties.name: Sigurd and Fafnir
properties.summary: The hero Sigurd, guided by the smith Regin, slew the dragon Fafnir and bathed in its blood, gaining near-invulnerability. He tasted the dragon's heart and could understand bird speech. He woke the Valkyrie Brynhild from her enchanted sleep. His story ends in betrayal and tragedy at the Burgundian court.

properties.name: Norse Creation â€” Ginnungagap
properties.summary: In the beginning was Ginnungagap, the yawning void between fire (Muspelheim) and ice (Niflheim). The frost giant Ymir formed from melting ice, nourished by the cosmic cow Audhumla. Odin and his brothers slew Ymir and fashioned the world from his body: his flesh became earth, blood became seas, skull became sky.

properties.name: Epic of Gilgamesh
properties.summary: King Gilgamesh of Uruk, two-thirds god, befriended the wild man Enkidu. Together they slew Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven. When Enkidu died, Gilgamesh sought immortality from flood-survivor Utnapishtim. He found the plant of youth but a serpent stole it. He returned home accepting mortality, his legacy being the walls of Uruk.

properties.name: Enuma Elish â€” Babylonian Creation
properties.summary: From the mixing of sweet water (Apsu) and salt water (Tiamat) came the first gods. When Apsu plotted to destroy them, Enki killed him. Tiamat raised an army of monsters. Marduk slew Tiamat, splitting her body to form heaven and earth. Humans were created from Kingu's blood to serve the gods.

properties.name: Ishtar's Descent to the Underworld
properties.summary: Ishtar descended through the seven gates of the underworld, removing one garment at each gate until she stood naked before her sister Ereshkigal, queen of the dead. The world above withered without her. She was rescued but had to send a substitute â€” her lover Tammuz, who would spend half the year below.

properties.name: The Great Flood (Utnapishtim)
properties.summary: The gods decided to destroy humanity with a flood. Enki warned Utnapishtim, who built a great boat and loaded it with animals and craftsmen. After seven days the flood subsided. Utnapishtim released a dove, swallow, and raven. The gods granted him immortality. This predates the biblical Noah story.

properties.name: Osiris, Isis, and Set
properties.summary: Set murdered his brother Osiris, dismembering and scattering his body across Egypt. Isis gathered the pieces and resurrected Osiris long enough to conceive Horus. Osiris became lord of the dead. Horus grew up to challenge Set, eventually winning kingship. This myth established the pharaonic succession pattern.

properties.name: Journey Through the Duat (Book of the Dead)
properties.summary: Each night Ra traveled through the twelve hours of the Duat (underworld), battling the serpent Apophis. Dead souls followed the same path, facing trials and gates guarded by demons. In the Hall of Two Truths, Anubis weighed the heart against Ma'at's feather. Ammit devoured those who failed.

properties.name: Creation by Atum at Heliopolis
properties.summary: Atum emerged from the primordial waters of Nun atop the first mound (benben). Through self-creation, he produced Shu (air) and Tefnut (moisture). They bore Geb (earth) and Nut (sky), who were separated by their father Shu. This Ennead of nine gods formed the basis of Egyptian cosmology.

properties.name: Mahabharata â€” Kurukshetra War
properties.summary: The great war between the Pandava and Kaurava cousins for the throne of Hastinapura lasted eighteen days. Krishna served as Arjuna's charioteer, delivering the Bhagavad Gita on the battlefield. The Pandavas won but at devastating cost, with almost all warriors dead. The epic addresses dharma, duty, and cosmic justice.

properties.name: Ramayana â€” Rama's Journey
properties.summary: Prince Rama was exiled for fourteen years with his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana. The demon king Ravana abducted Sita to Lanka. Rama allied with Hanuman and the monkey army, built a bridge across the ocean, and defeated Ravana. He returned to Ayodhya as king, celebrated as the festival Diwali.

properties.name: Churning of the Ocean of Milk
properties.summary: Devas and Asuras cooperated to churn the cosmic ocean using Mount Mandara as a churning rod and Vasuki the serpent as a rope. From the ocean emerged treasures: Lakshmi, the divine physician, the moon, and the elixir of immortality (amrita). Vishnu as Mohini tricked the Asuras to ensure only the Devas drank the amrita.

properties.name: Pangu Creates the World
properties.summary: Pangu was born inside a cosmic egg of chaos. He grew for 18,000 years, pushing heaven and earth apart. When he died, his body became the world: breath became wind, voice became thunder, eyes became sun and moon, blood became rivers, and parasites on his body became humanity.

properties.name: NÃ¼wa Creates Humanity
properties.summary: After Pangu created the world, the goddess NÃ¼wa was lonely. She shaped humans from yellow clay â€” carefully crafting nobles by hand and flinging drops of mud for commoners. She also repaired the sky when it was torn, using five colored stones. With her brother-husband Fuxi, she established marriage and civilization.

properties.name: Journey to the West â€” Monkey King
properties.summary: Sun Wukong, born from a stone egg, achieved immortality and wreaked havoc in Heaven before being imprisoned under a mountain by Buddha for 500 years. Released to accompany the monk Xuanzang on a pilgrimage to India for Buddhist scriptures, he protected the monk through 81 trials with his magical abilities.

properties.name: Izanagi and Izanami Create Japan
properties.summary: The divine couple Izanagi and Izanami stirred the cosmic ocean with a jeweled spear, and drops formed the Japanese islands. They created gods, but Izanami died giving birth to fire. Izanagi descended to Yomi (underworld) but fled in horror at her decayed form. Purifying himself, he birthed Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo.

properties.name: Amaterasu and the Cave
properties.summary: Offended by her brother Susanoo's violence, Amaterasu hid in a cave, plunging the world into darkness. The gods gathered outside, and Amenouzume performed an ecstatic dance that made them laugh. Curious, Amaterasu peeked out and was pulled into the light. The world was illuminated again.

properties.name: Dangun â€” Founding of Korea
properties.summary: Hwanung, son of the Lord of Heaven, descended to Mount Baekdu. A bear and tiger wished to become human. Given garlic and mugwort in a cave for 100 days, only the bear persevered, becoming a woman. She married Hwanung and bore Dangun, who founded Gojoseon (Old Korea) in 2333 BCE.

properties.name: Five Suns â€” Aztec Creation Cycles
properties.summary: The Aztec cosmos underwent five creations (Suns), each destroyed by a different cataclysm. The first by jaguars, second by wind, third by fire-rain, fourth by flood. In the fifth (current) Sun, the humble god Nanahuatzin sacrificed himself by jumping into fire to become the sun, requiring blood sacrifice to maintain its movement.

properties.name: Popol Vuh â€” Hero Twins
properties.summary: The Hero Twins, Hunahpu and Xbalanque, descended to the underworld Xibalba to avenge their father. Through cleverness they defeated the Lords of Death in ball games and trials. They were sacrificed, ground up, and thrown into a river, but regenerated. They tricked the lords into being sacrificed and rose as the sun and moon.

properties.name: Viracocha Creates the World
properties.summary: Viracocha rose from Lake Titicaca and created the sun, moon, and stars. He fashioned humans from stone but was unsatisfied. He caused a great flood, then created humans again from clay, giving each nation its language, songs, and customs. He walked across the Pacific and vanished, promising to return.

properties.name: Perun vs Veles
properties.summary: The thunder god Perun eternally battles the chthonic serpent-god Veles, who steals cattle, water, or Perun's wife from the heavens. Perun hurls lightning to strike Veles, who hides in trees, animals, or water. The cycle of theft and retribution mirrors the seasonal cycle and the cosmic order.

properties.name: Ergenekon â€” Birth of the Turks
properties.summary: After a devastating defeat, the last surviving Turks fled to the mythical Ergenekon valley, surrounded by impassable mountains. For generations they lived in isolation. When they grew too numerous, a blacksmith melted the iron mountain with a great fire, and a grey wolf (Bozkurt) led them out to conquer the steppe.

properties.name: Seven Labors of Rostam
properties.summary: The greatest hero of Persian legend, Rostam, completed seven impossible tasks to rescue King Kavus: slaying a lion, surviving the desert, defeating a dragon, overcoming a sorceress, capturing a demon, surviving a storm, and slaying the White Demon. His tragic fate was killing his own son Sohrab in battle.

properties.name: Maui Fishes Up Islands & Snares the Sun
properties.summary: The demigod Maui was a supreme trickster. He fished up the North Island of New Zealand using his grandmother's jawbone as a hook. He snared the sun with ropes to slow its journey and give people more daylight. He stole fire from the underworld goddess Mahuika. He died attempting to win immortality by crawling through the goddess of death.

properties.name: The Rainbow Serpent
properties.summary: In the Dreamtime, the Rainbow Serpent slithered across the flat land, creating rivers, valleys, and ridges with its massive body. It established the laws of behavior and consequence. Those who obey prosper; those who break the law are turned to stone. It still sleeps in waterways, maintaining the natural order.

properties.name: Creation of the World (Yoruba)
properties.summary: Olodumare sent Obatala to create land by pouring sand from a snail shell onto the primordial ocean. A chicken scratched the sand to spread it, forming land. Obatala shaped humans from clay but got drunk on palm wine, creating those with disabilities. Oduduwa completed the task, founding Ile-Ife, the sacred city.

properties.name: Forging of the Sampo
properties.summary: The eternal sage VÃ¤inÃ¤mÃ¶inen commissioned the smith Ilmarinen to forge the Sampo, a magical artifact that produced flour, salt, and gold. It was given to Louhi, mistress of Pohjola (the North), as a bride-price. When VÃ¤inÃ¤mÃ¶inen, Ilmarinen, and LemminkÃ¤inen attempted to steal it back, the Sampo was shattered in a sea battle.

properties.name: Coyote Steals Fire
properties.summary: In many Native American traditions, Coyote stole fire from the Fire Spirits to give to humanity. Through cunning and relay races with other animals, the fire was passed until it reached humanity. Coyote's cleverness is balanced by his foolishness. He is both creator and destroyer, teacher and troublemaker.

properties.name: CÃº Chulainn's Defense of Ulster
properties.summary: When Queen Medb of Connacht invaded Ulster to steal the Brown Bull, the teenage hero CÃº Chulainn single-handedly defended the province at a ford, fighting champions in single combat for months due to a curse on the Ulster warriors. His battle frenzy (rÃ­astrad) transformed him into a terrifying creature.

properties.name: Amirani â€” Georgian Prometheus
properties.summary: Amirani, son of a goddess, stole fire from the heavens and gave it to humanity. As punishment, he was chained to a rock in the Caucasus Mountains where an eagle eternally pecks at his heart. He still struggles to break free, causing earthquakes. The parallel with Prometheus is striking and ancient.

properties.name: Song of Kumarbi â€” Divine Succession
properties.summary: Alalu was overthrown by Anu (heaven), who was overthrown by Kumarbi, who bit off and swallowed Anu's genitals. From this act, the storm god Teshub was born and eventually defeated Kumarbi. This divine succession myth closely parallels the Greek Theogony's account of Kronos and Zeus.

properties.name: Baal Cycle â€” Storm vs Sea vs Death
properties.summary: Baal, storm god of the Canaanites, defeated Yamm (Sea) to establish order. He then confronted Mot (Death) and was killed, descending to the underworld. His sister-consort Anat defeated Mot, and Baal was resurrected. The cycle repeats with the seasons, ensuring agriculture and cosmic balance.

properties.name: David of Sassoun
properties.summary: The Armenian national epic tells of four generations of heroes from Sassoun. David, the greatest, wielded a magical sword and rode a supernatural horse. He defeated the tyrannical Msra Melik and liberated his people. His grandson Mher was trapped inside a rock for eternity, emerging only when the world becomes worthy.

properties.name: Shango â€” Lord of Thunder
properties.summary: Shango was a powerful king of Oyo who wielded thunder and fire. Betrayed by his subjects, he hanged himself but was deified as the orisha of thunder and justice. His three wives â€” Oya (wind), Oba (river), and Oshun (fertility) â€” became powerful orishas themselves. He is invoked for justice and strength.

properties.name: The Blue Wolf and the Fallow Doe
properties.summary: The Mongol people descended from BÃ¶rte Chino (Blue Wolf) who mated with Gua Maral (Fallow Doe) after crossing the sea. Their offspring populated the steppe and eventually produced Genghis Khan, who united the Mongol tribes under Eternal Blue Heaven's mandate. The wolf remains a sacred ancestor symbol.

properties.name: Apedemak the Lion God
properties.summary: Apedemak, the lion-headed warrior god of Kush, was worshipped as the supreme war deity. His temple at Naqa features him dispensing prisoners to the Meroitic king. The warrior queen Amanirenas invoked Apedemak when she led Kushite armies against Roman Egypt, famously losing an eye in battle but winning favorable terms.

properties.name: Jataka Tales â€” Buddha's Past Lives
properties.summary: The Jataka tales recount over 500 previous lives of the Buddha as he accumulated merit toward enlightenment. In various incarnations as animals, kings, and ordinary people, the Bodhisattva demonstrated compassion, generosity, and wisdom. The stories teach moral lessons through allegory and adventure.

properties.name: Etruscan Afterlife Banquet
properties.summary: Etruscan tomb paintings depict joyful afterlife banquets where the deceased feast, dance, and enjoy music in the presence of guardian spirits. Vanth, a winged female figure, guided souls. Charun, with his hammer, guarded the underworld gate. The Etruscans viewed death as a transition to continued celebration.

properties.name: Quetzalcoatl's Exile
properties.summary: Quetzalcoatl, the Feathered Serpent, ruled as a wise priest-king of Tula. His rival Tezcatlipoca tricked him into drunkenness and sin. Ashamed, Quetzalcoatl exiled himself, sailing east on a raft of serpents, vowing to return. This prophecy later played into the Spanish conquest when CortÃ©s was initially mistaken for the returning god.

properties.name: Ahura Mazda vs Angra Mainyu
properties.summary: Ahura Mazda (Wise Lord) created the world from pure thought. His adversary Angra Mainyu (Destructive Spirit) corrupted creation with disease, death, and evil. History is the 12,000-year cosmic battle between truth (asha) and falsehood (druj). At the end, a Saoshyant (savior) will purify the world in molten metal, defeating evil forever.

properties.name: Deucalion's Flood
properties.summary: Zeus sent a flood to destroy corrupt humanity. Deucalion and Pyrrha survived on a chest, landing on Mount Parnassus. They repopulated the earth by throwing stones over their shoulders â€” stones became people. This Greek flood narrative parallels the older Mesopotamian version closely.

properties.name: Theseus and the Minotaur
properties.summary: Athens was forced to send seven youths and seven maidens to Crete to feed the Minotaur in the Labyrinth. Prince Theseus volunteered, aided by Ariadne's thread to navigate the maze. He slew the beast and freed Athens from the tribute. He abandoned Ariadne on Naxos.

properties.name: Perseus and Medusa
properties.summary: Perseus was sent to kill Medusa, the Gorgon whose gaze turned people to stone. Aided by Athena's mirror shield, Hermes' winged sandals, and Hades' cap of invisibility, he beheaded Medusa while looking at her reflection. He used her head to rescue Andromeda from a sea monster.

properties.name: Jason and the Golden Fleece
properties.summary: Jason assembled the Argonauts to retrieve the Golden Fleece from Colchis. They faced clashing rocks, harpies, and fire-breathing bulls. Medea, the sorceress princess, helped Jason succeed out of love. Their return and tragic aftermath â€” Medea's revenge â€” remains one of mythology's darkest tales.

properties.name: Oedipus and the Sphinx
properties.summary: Oedipus unknowingly fulfilled a prophecy by killing his father and marrying his mother. He first proved his wisdom by solving the Sphinx's riddle. When the truth was revealed, Jocasta hanged herself and Oedipus blinded himself. Fate proved inescapable despite every human effort.

properties.name: Thor vs JÃ¶rmungandr
properties.summary: Thor and the Midgard Serpent JÃ¶rmungandr are fated enemies. Thor once nearly caught the serpent while fishing with the giant Hymir, using an ox head as bait. At RagnarÃ¶k, they will fight to their mutual destruction â€” Thor slays the serpent but falls dead from its venom after nine steps.

properties.name: Loki's Mischief and Punishment
properties.summary: Loki, the trickster god, caused endless trouble â€” cutting Thor's wife's hair, tricking blind HÃ¶Ã°r into killing the beloved Balder, and scheming against the gods. Finally bound with serpent venom dripping on his face, he will break free at RagnarÃ¶k to lead the forces of chaos.

properties.name: Death of Balder
properties.summary: Balder, the most beloved god, had prophetic nightmares of death. Frigg extracted oaths from all things not to harm him â€” except mistletoe. Loki fashioned a mistletoe dart and guided blind HÃ¶Ã°r to throw it, killing Balder. The gods tried to ransom him from Hel but Loki refused to weep, sealing Balder's death.

properties.name: Manu and the Great Flood
properties.summary: Manu, the first man, found a small fish that was Vishnu's avatar Matsya. The fish warned of a coming flood and instructed Manu to build a boat. When the flood came, Matsya grew enormous and towed the boat to safety on a mountain peak. Manu repopulated the earth through sacrifice and prayer.

properties.name: Krishna's Divine Play (Lila)
properties.summary: Born in a prison to defeat the tyrant Kamsa, Krishna was raised among cowherds. He performed miracles â€” lifting Mount Govardhana, dancing with the gopis, and playing enchanting flute. His love with Radha represents the soul's longing for the divine. He later served as Arjuna's charioteer in the Mahabharata.

properties.name: Pralaya â€” Cosmic Dissolution
properties.summary: Hindu cosmology envisions vast cycles of creation and destruction. Each cosmic day of Brahma (kalpa) spans 4.32 billion years. At the end, Shiva dances the Tandava, dissolving the universe. Vishnu sleeps on the cosmic serpent Shesha in primordial waters. From his navel grows a lotus bearing Brahma, who creates anew.

properties.name: Chang'e Flies to the Moon
properties.summary: The archer Hou Yi shot down nine of ten suns that were scorching the earth. He received the elixir of immortality but his wife Chang'e drank it and floated to the moon, where she lives forever with the Jade Rabbit. The Mid-Autumn Festival commemorates their eternal separation.

properties.name: Four Dragon Kings of the Seas
properties.summary: Four Dragon Kings rule the four seas surrounding China, controlling rain and weather. When they defied the Jade Emperor to bring rain to drought-stricken humans, they were transformed into four great rivers. The Dragon Kings' underwater crystal palaces are settings for many Chinese legends.

properties.name: Susanoo Slays Yamata no Orochi
properties.summary: The storm god Susanoo, banished from heaven for his wild behavior, encountered an old couple weeping over their daughter Kushinadahime, the last of eight daughters devoured by an eight-headed serpent. Susanoo got the serpent drunk on sake, then slew it. From its tail he drew the sword Kusanagi, one of Japan's imperial regalia.

properties.name: The Fox Wife (Kitsune)
properties.summary: A beautiful woman married a man and bore his child. One night, startled by a dog, she revealed her true form â€” a fox spirit (kitsune). Though she loved her family, she was forced to leave, visiting only in dreams. Foxes with multiple tails possess greater power, with nine-tailed foxes being near-divine.

properties.name: Gumiho â€” Nine-Tailed Fox
properties.summary: The gumiho is a fox that has lived a thousand years, gaining the ability to transform into a beautiful woman. Unlike Japanese kitsune, Korean gumiho are typically malevolent, consuming the livers or hearts of men. Some stories tell of gumiho who genuinely fall in love and seek to become fully human through restraint.

properties.name: Maya Creation â€” Maize People
properties.summary: The creator gods tried three times to make humans. Mud people dissolved, wood people were hollow and soulless. Finally, Xmucane ground white and yellow maize into dough, creating humans with blood and maize flesh. These humans were perfect â€” too perfect, so the gods clouded their vision to maintain divine authority.

properties.name: Baba Yaga and Vasilisa
properties.summary: Orphaned Vasilisa was sent by her stepmother to fetch fire from Baba Yaga, the fearsome witch who lives in a hut on chicken legs, surrounded by a fence of bones. Using her dead mother's magical doll for guidance, Vasilisa completed impossible tasks and obtained fire that burned her cruel stepfamily.

properties.name: Book of Dede Korkut
properties.summary: The epic tales of Dede Korkut recount the adventures of Oghuz Turkish heroes. Bamsi Beyrek endures trials to marry his beloved. Kan Turali fights monsters to win a warrior princess. The wise bard Dede Korkut advises and narrates, his songs shaping destiny. Each tale upholds honor, bravery, and loyalty.

properties.name: Anansi the Spider
properties.summary: Anansi the Spider wanted to own all stories. The sky god Nyame set impossible prices: capture Onini the python, Osebo the leopard, Mmoboro the hornets, and Mmoatia the invisible fairy. Through cunning rather than strength, Anansi captured them all. Nyame made all stories 'spider stories' (Anansesem).

properties.name: Raven Steals the Light
properties.summary: In the beginning, the world was dark. The Sky Chief kept the sun, moon, and stars in bentwood boxes. Raven transformed into a pine needle, was swallowed by the chief's daughter, and was reborn as her grandson. As a child, he opened the boxes one by one, releasing light into the world.

properties.name: White Buffalo Calf Woman
properties.summary: Two Lakota warriors encountered a beautiful woman in white. One approached with desire and was reduced to bones. The other was respectful. She brought the sacred pipe (chanunpa), teaching seven sacred rites including the Sun Dance, vision quest, and sweat lodge. She transformed into a white buffalo calf and vanished.

properties.name: VÃ¤inÃ¤mÃ¶inen's Creation Song
properties.summary: The goddess Ilmatar lay floating on the primordial ocean. A teal laid seven eggs on her knee; they broke and formed the earth, sky, sun, and moon. From the waters VÃ¤inÃ¤mÃ¶inen was born, an ancient sage who sang the world into being. His songs had the power to reshape reality itself.

properties.name: Tlaloc and the Rain Sacrifice
properties.summary: Tlaloc, the rain god, dwelt atop mountain peaks and in caves where clouds formed. He brought sustaining rain but also destructive storms, hail, and floods. Child sacrifices were offered to Tlaloc, their tears believed to bring rain. His paradise, Tlalocan, received those who died by water or lightning.

properties.name: Inti Raymi â€” Festival of the Sun
properties.summary: Each winter solstice, the Inca held Inti Raymi, fearing the sun might not return. The Sapa Inca fasted, then led elaborate ceremonies with sacrifices, music, and feasting. Sacred flames were kindled with mirrors, and chicha (corn beer) was offered. The festival reinforced the Sapa Inca's divine solar lineage.

properties.name: Separation of Rangi and Papa
properties.summary: Sky Father Rangi and Earth Mother Papa lay locked in eternal embrace, trapping their children in darkness. The children debated how to separate them. Tane Mahuta, god of forests, pushed them apart with his legs. Tawhirimatea, god of storms, was furious and attacked his brothers. Rangi's tears became rain.

properties.name: Sedna â€” Mistress of the Sea
properties.summary: Sedna was a beautiful Inuit woman tricked into marrying a bird spirit. Her father Anguta rescued her by kayak, but a storm threatened to capsize them. He threw Sedna overboard; when she clung to the boat, he cut off her fingers. Her fingers became seals, walruses, and whales. She sank to rule the sea floor.

properties.name: The Songlines â€” Walking the Dreaming
properties.summary: During the Dreaming, Ancestor Beings walked across Australia singing the world into existence. Each feature â€” rock, waterhole, hill â€” was created by their songs. Aboriginal people maintain these songlines as navigational paths, spiritual practices, and legal codes. Walking a songline connects past creation with present reality.

properties.name: Journey to Mictlan
properties.summary: After death, most Aztec souls traveled to Mictlan through nine challenging layers over four years. They crossed rivers of blood, passed between clashing mountains, endured razor-sharp winds, and finally stood before the death lord Mictlantecuhtli. A hairless dog (xoloitzcuintli) guided the soul through the underworld.

properties.name: VÃ¤inÃ¤mÃ¶inen's Journey to Tuonela
properties.summary: VÃ¤inÃ¤mÃ¶inen journeyed to Tuonela, the Finnish underworld, seeking magical knowledge. He crossed the dark river and was received by the death goddess Tuonetar, who offered him beer of forgetfulness. Iron nets were cast to trap him. Using his shape-shifting powers, VÃ¤inÃ¤mÃ¶inen escaped as a snake, warning others never to visit Tuonela voluntarily.

properties.name: Purusha Sacrifice â€” Vedic Creation
properties.summary: The cosmic being Purusha was sacrificed by the gods. From his body, the world was created: his mouth became brahmins, arms became warriors, thighs became merchants, feet became servants. From his mind came the moon, eyes the sun, breath the wind. This primordial sacrifice established cosmic and social order.

properties.name: Creation by Eternal Blue Heaven
properties.summary: Eternal Blue Heaven (MÃ¶ngke Tengri) created the world from primordial waters. He sent a duck to dive for mud from the ocean floor; from this mud he shaped the earth. The devil figure Erlik created mountains and swamps as obstacles. Tengri breathed soul into humans, while Erlik gave them disease and death.

properties.name: Rod Creates the Universe
properties.summary: Rod, the supreme creator, broke the cosmic egg to create the universe. Light and darkness, earth and sky separated. He created Svarog the sky-smith who forged the sun. The Rozhanitsy (Rod's daughters) wove the fates of all living beings. Rod breathed life into everything and retired to the highest heaven.

properties.name: Tengri and the World Tree
properties.summary: The Turkic cosmos is organized around a great World Tree connecting three realms: the upper sky-realm of Tengri, the middle world of humans, and the lower realm of Erlik. Shamans climb the tree in trance to communicate between worlds. Sixteen-layered heavens and seven-layered underworld contain various spirits.

properties.name: Phoenician Cosmogony
properties.summary: From primordial dark wind and chaos, Mot (a cosmic egg of mud) cracked open. Sun, moon, and stars emerged. Animals and then humans appeared on the shores of Phoenicia. El, the father of gods, established divine order. The craftsman god Kothar-wa-Khasis fashioned divine tools and temples.

properties.name: The Dragon Illuyanka
properties.summary: The Storm God was defeated by the dragon Illuyanka, who stole his heart and eyes. The goddess Inaras seduced Illuyanka with a feast, getting him drunk so a mortal could bind him. In another version, the Storm God's son married Illuyanka's daughter and recovered the organs, allowing his father to triumph.

properties.name: Jebel Barkal â€” Sacred Mountain of Creation
properties.summary: The Nubians believed Jebel Barkal was the primordial mound of creation where the god Amun dwelt inside the mountain. A natural rock pinnacle resembled a uraeus (royal cobra), confirming divine presence. This sacred geography legitimized Kushite kings as true pharaohs, heirs to the original creation.

properties.name: Birth of Vahagn the Dragon-Slayer
properties.summary: Vahagn was born from cosmic fire â€” heaven and earth labored, the sea turned red, and from a reed stalk fire emerged, forming a golden-haired youth with eyes like suns. He slew dragons (vishaps) and stole hay from the Milky Way (the 'Straw-Thief's Way' in Armenian). He was Armenia's war god.

properties.name: The Golden Fleece in Colchis
properties.summary: In Georgian tradition, King Aeetes of Colchis guarded the Golden Fleece â€” the skin of a divine ram that had rescued children from sacrifice. The fleece hung in a sacred grove guarded by a dragon. When Jason came with the Argonauts, Aeetes' daughter Medea betrayed her father out of love. The story reflects Colchis's historical gold wealth.

properties.name: Metamorphoses â€” Tales of Transformation
properties.summary: Ovid's Metamorphoses weaves 250 transformation myths into a continuous narrative from creation to Julius Caesar's apotheosis. Narcissus becomes a flower, Daphne a laurel tree, Arachne a spider, and Icarus falls from the sky. Each transformation reveals the consequences of hubris, desire, or divine whim.

properties.name: Roman Creation â€” Ages of Man
properties.summary: The Roman creation myth describes four ages: the Golden Age under Saturn, when the earth yielded crops without labor; the Silver Age; the Bronze Age of warfare; and the Iron Age of suffering. Each age saw moral decline. Saturn's Golden Age became the model for the Saturnalia festival.

properties.name: The Quest for the Holy Grail
properties.summary: King Arthur's knights of the Round Table embarked on the quest for the Holy Grail, the cup used by Christ at the Last Supper. Only the pure-hearted Galahad succeeded, while Lancelot was denied for his adultery with Guinevere. The quest reveals each knight's spiritual worth and the limits of martial valor.

properties.name: OisÃ­n in TÃ­r na nÃ“g
properties.summary: The warrior OisÃ­n fell in love with Niamh of the Golden Hair, who brought him to TÃ­r na nÃ“g (Land of the Young). He lived there for what seemed three years but was actually 300. Returning to Ireland, he was forbidden to touch the ground. When he fell from his horse, he aged instantly into an old man.

properties.name: Tale of Chunhyang
properties.summary: Chunhyang, the daughter of a gisaeng (courtesan), secretly married the nobleman's son Mongryong. When Mongryong left for Seoul, the corrupt governor Byeon Hakdo tried to force Chunhyang to be his concubine. She refused and was tortured. Mongryong returned as a secret royal inspector and saved her. Their love transcended class.

properties.name: Tages Rises from the Furrow
properties.summary: While plowing a field near Tarquinia, a farmer's plow uncovered a child with the wisdom of an elder. This was Tages, a divine being who taught the Etruscans the art of haruspicy (reading entrails), the interpretation of lightning, and the sacred laws (Etrusca disciplina). He then vanished.

properties.name: Pandora's Box
properties.summary: Zeus created Pandora, the first woman, as punishment for Prometheus's theft of fire. Each god gave her gifts â€” beauty, cunning, curiosity. She was given a jar (pithos) and told never to open it. Curiosity overwhelmed her, releasing all evils into the world. Only Hope remained inside.

properties.name: Echo and Narcissus
properties.summary: The beautiful Narcissus rejected all lovers, including the nymph Echo who faded to only a voice. Nemesis cursed him to fall in love with his own reflection. Unable to look away from the pool, Narcissus wasted away and was transformed into the flower bearing his name.

properties.name: The Trojan Horse
properties.summary: After ten years besieging Troy, the Greeks built a hollow wooden horse and hid warriors inside. They feigned retreat. Despite LaocoÃ¶n's warning, the Trojans brought the horse inside their walls. At night, Greek soldiers emerged and opened the gates. Troy burned in a single devastating night.

properties.name: Theft of the Mead of Poetry
properties.summary: The Mead of Poetry was brewed from the blood of the wisest being, Kvasir. Odin infiltrated the giant Suttung's mountain by seducing his daughter GunnlÃ¶Ã°. He drank all three cauldrons of mead and escaped as an eagle, spitting the mead into vessels in Asgard. Some spilled to earth, giving mortals poetry.

properties.name: Narasimha â€” The Man-Lion Avatar
properties.summary: The demon king Hiranyakashipu received a boon: he could not be killed by man or animal, inside or outside, by day or night. He terrorized his devoted son Prahlada who worshipped Vishnu. Vishnu appeared as Narasimha (half-man, half-lion) at twilight, on a threshold, and killed the demon on his lap.

properties.name: Fu Xi and the Eight Trigrams
properties.summary: The sage-emperor Fu Xi observed patterns in nature â€” the markings on a dragon-horse, turtle shells, and the stars. He devised the eight trigrams (bagua), capturing the fundamental principles of reality: heaven, earth, fire, water, mountain, lake, wind, and thunder. These became the basis of the I Ching.

properties.name: Yu the Great Controls the Flood
properties.summary: Great floods threatened China. Yu's father Gun tried to stop them by stealing magic soil from heaven. He failed. Yu spent thirteen years channeling the waters through drainage, never visiting home even when passing by. He divided the land into nine provinces and became the first emperor of the Xia dynasty.

properties.name: Tanabata â€” The Star-Crossed Lovers
properties.summary: Orihime (Vega) wove beautiful cloth for her father the Sky King. She fell in love with the cowherd Hikoboshi (Altair). They neglected their work, so the Sky King separated them on opposite sides of the Milky Way. They may meet only once a year on the seventh of July, when magpies form a bridge.

properties.name: Urashima TarÅ â€” The Fisherman's Journey
properties.summary: Fisherman Urashima TarÅ rescued a turtle, which took him to the Dragon Palace under the sea. He married the princess Otohime and lived happily for three days. Returning home, he found 300 years had passed. He opened a forbidden box she gave him and aged instantly to dust.

properties.name: The Flood of the Wood People
properties.summary: In the second creation, the gods made humans from wood. These people could speak but lacked hearts and minds, showing no gratitude to their creators. The gods sent a great flood of black rain and resin. Animals and even their own tools attacked the wood people. Their descendants became monkeys.

properties.name: The Rusalki â€” Water Spirits
properties.summary: Rusalki are water spirits â€” souls of young women who died violently near water. They emerge during Rusalka Week in early summer, dancing in moonlit meadows and forests. Their beauty enchants young men, whom they lure into rivers to drown. Green wreaths and garlic protect against them.

properties.name: Alp Er Tunga â€” The Great King
properties.summary: Alp Er Tunga (identified with the Persian Afrasiyab) was a legendary Turkic king who waged wars against Iran. His death was sung in elegies across the Turkic world. Mahmud of Kashgar recorded mourning poems in the Divan. He represented the ideal Turkic ruler â€” brave, just, and fierce in battle.

properties.name: Zal and the Simorgh
properties.summary: Zal, born with white hair, was abandoned on Mount Damavand by his ashamed father Sam. The Simorgh, a benevolent mythical bird, raised him. When Sam repented, the Simorgh returned Zal with one of her feathers â€” when burned, she would come to his aid. Zal married Rudabeh and fathered the hero Rostam.

properties.name: Buddha's Enlightenment â€” Temptation by Mara
properties.summary: Under the Bodhi tree, Siddhartha meditated for 49 days seeking enlightenment. Mara, lord of illusion, attacked him with armies, tempted him with beautiful daughters, and challenged his right to awaken. Siddhartha touched the earth, calling it as witness. Mara fled, and Siddhartha became the Buddha â€” the Awakened One.

properties.name: Pele â€” Goddess of Volcanoes
properties.summary: Pele traveled across the Pacific creating volcanic islands until she settled in Hawaii's KÄ«lauea. She is both creator and destroyer â€” lava from her anger forms new land. Her rivalry with the pig god Kamapua'a and her love for the mortal Lohiau drive dramatic narratives. She is a living deity still honored today.

properties.name: How Fire Was Stolen (Aboriginal)
properties.summary: In various Aboriginal traditions, fire was guarded by selfish keepers. Crow (or other clever animals) devised schemes to steal it for the people. In one version, Crow tricked the fire-keepers into opening their sacred box, grabbed a burning stick, and flew away, scorching his feathers permanently black.

properties.name: Ifa Divination â€” Orunmila's Gift
properties.summary: Orunmila, the orisha of wisdom, witnessed creation and knows the destiny of all beings. He gave humanity the Ifa divination system â€” 256 odu (signs) containing stories, medicines, and wisdom for every life situation. A babalawo (priest) casts palm nuts or chains to read destiny. Eshu carries messages between humans and orishas.

properties.name: The Shaman's Journey to the Sky
properties.summary: Mongolian shamans enter ecstatic trance, their soul traveling up the World Tree or riding spirit horses to reach the sky realms. They pass through nine or thirteen heavens to petition Tengri for healing, rain, or guidance. The shaman's drum is their spirit horse, and their costume represents the cosmos.

properties.name: The Warrior Queens (Kandakes)
properties.summary: The Kandakes (warrior queens) of Kush were both political rulers and living goddesses. Amanirenas led armies against Augustus's Rome, blinding herself in battle. Amanishakheto accumulated enormous treasure. They ruled with divine authority from Apedemak, building pyramids and temples that rivaled Egypt's achievements.

properties.name: Pachamama â€” Earth Mother
properties.summary: Pachamama is the living earth, a nurturing goddess who provides food, water, and shelter. In return, she demands respect and offerings (despachos). She can cause earthquakes when angry. During planting and harvest, chicha and coca leaves are offered. She is not merely a nature goddess â€” she IS the earth, alive and conscious.

properties.name: The Descent to Xibalba
properties.summary: Hun Hunahpu and his twin descended to Xibalba, the underworld, summoned by the Lords of Death who were angered by their ball-playing. They failed the tests â€” the Dark House, Cold House, Jaguar House, Fire House, and Bat House. They were sacrificed, and Hun Hunahpu's head was placed in a calabash tree.

properties.name: Yima's Vara â€” Persian Flood Myth
properties.summary: Ahura Mazda warned King Yima of a coming winter that would destroy all life. He instructed Yima to build a vara (enclosure) and fill it with the finest specimens of every living thing â€” seeds, animals, and humans. After the great winter passed, Yima's vara repopulated the world.

properties.name: Navajo Emergence â€” Four Worlds
properties.summary: The Navajo people emerged through four colored worlds â€” Black, Blue, Yellow, and White. In each world, conflicts caused by Coyote forced migration upward. Spider Woman taught weaving; First Man and First Woman brought sacred medicine bundles. Through a reed, the people climbed into the Fifth World â€” the present glittering world.

properties.name: Zhurong vs Gonggong â€” Battle of Fire and Water
properties.summary: The fire god Zhurong battled the water god Gonggong for supremacy. Defeated, Gonggong smashed his head against Mount Buzhou, one of the pillars holding up the sky. The sky tilted, causing floods and fires. NÃ¼wa repaired the sky with five-colored stones and cut off a turtle's legs as new pillars.

properties.name: Princess Pyeonggang and the Fool Ondal
properties.summary: The spirited princess cried so much that her father promised her to the village fool Ondal. She left the palace and married him, training him in martial arts and scholarship. Ondal became the nation's greatest general, proving that talent and love transcend social status. He died in battle defending the kingdom.

properties.name: The Birth of Ganesha
properties.summary: Parvati created a boy from turmeric paste to guard her bath. When Shiva returned and the boy blocked him, Shiva beheaded him in rage. Parvati's grief was so great that Shiva promised to restore the child with the head of the first creature found â€” an elephant. Thus Ganesha was born, remover of obstacles and lord of beginnings.

properties.name: The MorrÃ­gan â€” Phantom Queen of Battle
properties.summary: The MorrÃ­gan is a triple goddess of war, fate, and death. She appears as a crow over battlefields, selecting who will die. She offered CÃº Chulainn her love, and when refused, became his enemy â€” yet also his protector. Before battles, she washed the armor of those fated to die at the ford.

properties.name: Huitzilopochtli vs Coyolxauhqui
properties.summary: Coatlicue became pregnant from a ball of feathers. Her daughter Coyolxauhqui and 400 brothers plotted to kill her in shame. At the moment of attack, Huitzilopochtli was born fully armed, dismembering Coyolxauhqui and hurling her down Mount Coatepec. This battle is reenacted daily as the sun defeats the moon and stars.

properties.name: Proserpina and the Pomegranate
properties.summary: Pluto abducted Proserpina to the underworld. Her mother Ceres caused all plants to die. Jupiter brokered a deal but Proserpina had eaten pomegranate seeds â€” binding her to six months below. Her annual return brings spring; her departure brings winter. The Eleusinian-style mysteries spread this cult across the Roman Empire.

properties.name: LemminkÃ¤inen's Death and Resurrection
properties.summary: The reckless hero LemminkÃ¤inen was killed trying to shoot the swan of Tuonela. His body was hacked to pieces and thrown into the river of the dead. His mother, sensing his death, raked the river with a copper rake, gathered every fragment, and sang him back to life â€” the power of a mother's love and magic defeating death.

properties.name: Daedalus and Icarus
properties.summary: The master craftsman Daedalus built the Labyrinth for King Minos, then was imprisoned with his son Icarus. He crafted wings from feathers and wax. He warned Icarus not to fly too high or too low. Icarus, exhilarated, soared toward the sun. The wax melted and he fell into the sea.

properties.name: Freyja and the BrÃ­singamen
properties.summary: Freyja desired the BrÃ­singamen, a necklace of incomparable beauty forged by four dwarves. She spent a night with each dwarf to obtain it. Loki stole it on Odin's orders, transforming into a flea to unpin the clasp. Heimdall fought Loki to recover it. The necklace became Freyja's most treasured possession.

properties.name: The Destruction of Mankind (Sekhmet)
properties.summary: Ra sent his eye (Hathor/Sekhmet) to punish disobedient humanity. The lioness goddess Sekhmet went on a blood-fueled rampage, threatening to destroy all humans. To stop her, the gods dyed beer red with ochre to resemble blood. Sekhmet drank it, became drunk, and fell asleep, transforming back into gentle Hathor.

properties.name: Shiva's Cosmic Dance (Nataraja)
properties.summary: Shiva performs the Tandava, the cosmic dance that creates, sustains, and destroys the universe. As Nataraja (Lord of the Dance), he dances within a ring of fire. One foot crushes the dwarf Apasmara (ignorance), while the other is raised in liberation. His drum sounds creation, his fire hand destruction.

properties.name: Legend of the White Snake
properties.summary: A white snake spirit transformed into a beautiful woman and fell in love with the mortal Xu Xian. They married and she used her powers to help the sick. The monk Fahai exposed her true form and imprisoned her under Leifeng Pagoda. Green Snake eventually freed her. Their love transcended the boundary between human and spirit.

properties.name: MomotarÅ â€” The Peach Boy
properties.summary: An old childless couple found a giant peach floating down a river. Inside was a baby boy, MomotarÅ. He grew strong and journeyed to Onigashima (Demon Island) with a dog, monkey, and pheasant as companions. Together they defeated the oni and returned with treasure. MomotarÅ represents kindness and courage.

properties.name: The Firebird (Zhar-Ptitsa)
properties.summary: Prince Ivan pursued the Firebird that was stealing golden apples. Guided by a grey wolf, he endured trials â€” capturing the bird, stealing a golden horse, and rescuing a princess. His jealous brothers killed him, but the wolf brought him back to life. Ivan married the princess and claimed the kingdom.

properties.name: Kay Kavus Flies to Heaven
properties.summary: The vainglorious king Kay Kavus attempted to fly to heaven by harnessing eagles to his throne with meat tied above them on lances. The eagles flew upward seeking the meat. When exhausted, the eagles and throne crashed into a forest. Rostam had to rescue the humiliated king, as always.

properties.name: Avalokiteshvara and the Thousand Arms
properties.summary: The bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara vowed to free all beings from suffering. Looking upon the world, seeing endless pain, his head split into pieces from grief. Amitabha restored him with eleven heads to hear all cries and a thousand arms to reach all who suffer. In East Asia, Avalokiteshvara became Guanyin/Kannon.

properties.name: Kumulipo â€” Hawaiian Creation Chant
properties.summary: The Kumulipo is a 2,100-line creation chant linking the Hawaiian royal family to the origin of the cosmos. Creation proceeds from darkness to light, from coral and shellfish through fish, reptiles, birds, and finally humans. Each phase pairs male and female creative forces. The chant was performed at royal births.

properties.name: Corn Mother â€” Gift of Agriculture
properties.summary: In Penobscot tradition, Corn Mother arose from corn silk and married First Father. When famine came, she instructed her sons to kill her and drag her body over bare ground. From her flesh grew corn; from her bones grew tobacco. She sacrificed herself so her people would never go hungry.

properties.name: Rape of the Sabine Women
properties.summary: Early Rome had men but no women. Romulus invited the neighboring Sabines to a festival, then his men seized the women. War erupted between Romans and Sabines. The abducted women â€” now wives and mothers â€” threw themselves between the armies, demanding peace. The two peoples merged into one nation.

properties.name: Thoth Wins Five Days from the Moon
properties.summary: Ra cursed Nut that she could not give birth on any day of the year (then 360 days). Thoth, god of wisdom, gambled with the moon god Khonsu, winning moonlight to create five extra days outside the regular calendar. During these five intercalary days, Nut bore Osiris, Isis, Set, Nephthys, and Horus the Elder.

properties.name: Etana â€” The King Who Flew to Heaven
properties.summary: King Etana of Kish had no heir. An eagle, punished for betraying a serpent, was rescued by Etana in exchange for carrying him to heaven to find the Plant of Birth. Riding the eagle ever higher, Etana looked down and the earth shrank to nothing. Whether he succeeded remains unknown â€” the tablet is broken.

properties.name: Durga Slays Mahishasura
properties.summary: The buffalo demon Mahishasura received a boon that he could be killed by no god or man. He conquered the heavens. The gods combined their energies to create Durga, a goddess of supreme power. Each god gave her a weapon. After a nine-day battle, she slew Mahishasura, proving that divine feminine power surpasses all.

properties.name: Hou Yi Shoots Down Nine Suns
properties.summary: Ten sun-birds, sons of the sky god Di Jun, decided to cross the sky together, scorching the earth. The divine archer Hou Yi was sent to discipline them. When they refused to return, Hou Yi shot down nine suns, leaving one to light the world. Di Jun was furious and banished Hou Yi from heaven.

properties.name: Changsega â€” Korean Creation Epic
properties.summary: In the beginning, the giant Mireuk separated heaven and earth and placed four bronze pillars at the corners. He created the sun, moon, and stars from hanging lamps. A rival, Seokga, challenged him to a flower-growing contest. Seokga cheated, but won power over the human world, explaining why evil exists.

properties.name: Fionn and the Salmon of Knowledge
properties.summary: The druid Finnegas spent seven years fishing for the Salmon of Knowledge in the River Boyne. Young Fionn was tasked with cooking it but burned his thumb on the fish and instinctively sucked it. That taste gave him all the salmon's wisdom. Whenever he needed answers, he sucked his thumb to access infinite knowledge.

properties.name: Ogun Clears the Path to Earth
properties.summary: When the orishas descended from heaven to populate earth, the path was blocked by impenetrable forest. Only Ogun, god of iron, possessed the tools to cut through. He forged a machete and cleared the road. For this service, all orishas honored him. He became patron of blacksmiths, warriors, and all who use metal.

properties.name: The Seven Sisters (Pleiades)
properties.summary: Across Aboriginal Australia, the Pleiades are seven sisters fleeing a persistent hunter (Orion). They travel across the land, creating landmarks as they go. When he gets too close, they fly into the sky to escape. The hunter follows, forever chasing them across the heavens. The story maps onto real geography and star movements.

properties.name: Epic of King Gesar
properties.summary: King Gesar was sent from heaven to combat the demons infecting the human world. He was born miraculously, endured exile, and united the fractured tribes of Ling. Through martial prowess and divine wisdom, he defeated demon kings in all four directions. The longest epic in world literature â€” over a million verses in some versions.

properties.name: Antigone's Defiance
properties.summary: Antigone defied King Creon's edict by burying her brother Polynices, choosing divine law over human law. Creon sentenced her to death. She hanged herself, Creon's son Haemon killed himself at her tomb, and Creon's wife followed. Creon was left destroyed, learning too late that justice cannot be separated from mercy.

properties.name: Valhalla â€” Hall of the Slain
properties.summary: Warriors who died bravely in battle were chosen by the Valkyries to feast in Odin's great hall Valhalla. Each day they fought to the death, each evening they were resurrected to feast on the boar SÃ¦hrÃ­mnir and drink mead from the goat HeiÃ°rÃºn. They prepared for the final battle of RagnarÃ¶k.

properties.name: Ra's Nightly Journey Through the Duat
properties.summary: Each night, Ra sailed his barque through the twelve hours of the Duat (underworld). In the seventh hour, the chaos serpent Apophis attacked, threatening to swallow the sun forever. Set defended Ra, spearing the serpent. At dawn, Ra emerged reborn as Khepri, the scarab, ensuring another day for the living.

properties.name: Adapa and Immortality Lost
properties.summary: Adapa, a wise priest of Enki, broke the wing of the South Wind. Summoned before Anu in heaven, Enki warned him not to eat or drink anything offered. Anu, impressed by Adapa's wisdom, offered the food and water of immortality. Following Enki's advice, Adapa refused â€” and humanity lost its chance at eternal life.

properties.name: The Four Ayar Brothers
properties.summary: Four brothers and four sisters emerged from caves at Pacaritambo. The strongest brother, Ayar Cachi, was sealed in a cave by his jealous siblings because his sling could crumble mountains. One brother turned to stone as a boundary marker. Ayar Manco (Manco Capac) and Mama Ocllo finally founded Cusco.

properties.name: Hanuman's Leap to Lanka
properties.summary: The monkey god Hanuman, son of Vayu (Wind), volunteered to leap across the ocean to Lanka to find the captured Sita. He overcame Surasa, a sea demoness, and Simhika who tried to catch his shadow. He found Sita, delivered Rama's ring, set Lanka ablaze with his burning tail, and returned triumphant.

properties.name: Nezha Roils the Sea
properties.summary: Nezha was born from a flesh ball after three years' pregnancy. As a child, he killed the Dragon King's son while bathing in the sea, causing cosmic outrage. To save his parents from divine punishment, he carved his own flesh from his bones and returned it to them. His master resurrected him with lotus flowers.

properties.name: Crow and the Seven Emu Women
properties.summary: Crow was clever but hungry. He discovered the Emu Women had fire but wouldn't share. He prepared a fake wound full of ants and pretended to be injured. When the women came to help, he tricked them into gathering sticks. He stole their hidden firestick and flew away, but dropped embers across creation, giving fire to all.
